title: Print Window Page Break Shell Repeat And Part Suffix
description:
Make sure that elements when broken over multiple pages have the window shell repeated. E.g. when a window spans multiple pages then the complete window frame with chips etc is repeated on each page. Add a suffix ":" + part number to the hierarchy chip of the part, e.g. "Tabelle:1.2.3.4.a:1", "Tabelle:1.2.3.4.a:2" for the 2nd page-part of the same window. The parts should not show separately in the register/table list (e.g. Tabellenverzeichnis/listoftables) — the register entry should just show the base hierarchy path "1.2.3.4.a" once (no part suffix), not one entry per part.

Context: print/tex/semio-window.sty is the LaTeX "OS window chrome" component (tcolorbox-based). Currently `semio_window_tcb_open:n` (~line 850) always forces `breakable=false` for every window, so windows never split across pages today. Hierarchy chip numbering lives in print/tex/semio-core.sty (`\semio_kind_chip_number:nn`, `\semio_window_kind_number:n`, `\semio@hierarchy@path`) and print/tex/semio-window.sty (`\semio_window_kind_number_set:n`, `\semio_window_register_write:nn`, `\semio@heading@pair`). The register/TOC-style list machinery is the `\semio_window_register_write:nn` / `\semio_window_toc_append:*` / register-list `\listof*` pipeline in semio-window.sty.

Needs: (1) allow windows to become breakable across pages, (2) repeat the full window chrome (border, navbar/footer-style chip row, tab+hierarchy-chip pair) on every page the window's content spans, (3) track a per-window "part" counter that increments per page-continuation and append ":<part>" to the on-page hierarchy chip only for parts after the first (or design as fits — clarify during implementation) — but the register list entry written via semio_window_register_write:nn must be written once with the bare hierarchy path, no part suffix, and not duplicated per part.

Verify by building one of the real print templates/dist documents with a table/window long enough to span 2+ pages and inspecting the rendered PDF pages for repeated chrome + part-suffixed chips, plus confirming the table register list has a single non-suffixed entry.
summary:
Implemented window-shell page breaking + per-page-part hierarchy-chip suffix in print/tex/semio-window.sty, and verified with real tectonic builds + rasterized PDF inspection.

What changed (print/tex/semio-window.sty):
1. Breakable windows: removed the hardcoded `breakable=false` from `\semio_window_tcb_open:n` (both branches) and from the `semio~window~table` / `semio~window~row` tcbset styles, so a "kind" window (Table/Figure/etc., opened via `\semio_window_kind_begin:nnn`) now inherits real `breakable` from the base `semio~window` style (already `breakable`, via tcolorbox 5.0.2's `tcbuselibrary{skins,breakable,fitting}`). The generic `\Window` environment and `WindowRow`/`WindowColumn` arrangement primitives still explicitly pass `breakable=false` at their own `\begin{tcolorbox}` call sites (unrelated arrangement/layout primitives, out of scope), so they render unaffected.
2. Shell repeat on continuation pages: added `overlay unbroken=`, `overlay first=`, `overlay middle=`, `overlay last=` to the `semio~window` tcbset style. `overlay middle`/`overlay last` call new `\semio@window@header@repeat`, which redraws the exact existing header-chip routine (`\semio@window@header@muted`, same L-shape/cap/gap-paint code used for page 1) via a tikz node anchored to that page-part's own `frame` node (`at (frame.north)`, `anchor=south`, `yshift=\semio@stroke@hairline` to preserve the same border-overlap seam as the pre-box static header), appending the live `\arabic{tcbbreakpart}` part index. `overlay unbroken`/`overlay last` also call `\semio@window@break@record`, which writes the final part count into a new `.window-breaks` aux file (mirrors the existing `.register-toc` write-this-pass/read-next-pass convention), keyed by the window's bare register number.
3. Part-suffix two-pass mechanism: `\semio_window_break_suffix_apply:` (called right after `\semio_window_register_write:nn` in `\semio_window_kind_begin:nnn`) looks up the previous pass's recorded part count for this window (via new `\g_semio_window_break_prop`, loaded at `\AtBeginDocument` from `.window-breaks`) and sets `\g_semio_window_break_suffix_bool`. `\semio_window_header_store_aux:nn` uses that to build a separate `\semio@window@header@number@page1` macro (base number + ":1" only if flagged) used solely by the static pre-box header (`\semio@window@header@invoke`) — the bare `\semio@window@header@number` (no suffix) is what `\semio@window@header@repeat` reuses and appends its own live ":<N>" to, so page 1 never double-suffixes. `\l_semio_window_number_tl` / `\l_semio_window_register_number_tl` / `\g_semio_hierarchy_path_tl` are never touched, so `\label`/`\ref`/register-list numbers stay exactly the bare hierarchy path.
4. print/script.ts: added `.window-breaks` to `clearStaleTocAuxFiles`'s cleared extensions (same treatment as `.register-toc`) so each fresh build starts clean and tectonic's own `--reruns 2` converges the two-pass suffix data.

Bugs found and fixed along the way (both blocked ALL builds; unrelated to my feature but needed fixing to verify anything):
- A concurrent session's Glossary→Termlist refactor (already in the tree when I started) added `\semio_termlist_new:nnnn`, whose body ran `\makeatletter ... \makeatother` unwrapped by any TeX group at file top level — permanently flipping `@` to catcode "other" for the rest of package loading, breaking every later `\semio@...` control sequence. Fixed by wrapping that pair in `\group_begin:`/`\group_end:`.
- My own new macros initially failed similarly: `\ExplSyntaxOn` inside an already-tokenized `\newcommand` body doesn't retroactively fix tokenization, and `\ExplSyntaxOn` also makes space an ignored character (not just catcode 10) — explaining the file's existing `~`-for-space convention. Fixed by wrapping only the l3-calling macro's *definition* in ExplSyntaxOn, keeping the tikz-`\node`-using macro (needs real spaces) outside it.

Verification performed (real tectonic builds, not assumptions):
- `bunx nx run @semio-tech/print:test --skip-nx-cache` — all 12 template PDFs (6 templates × light/dark) build cleanly.
- `bunx nx run @semio-tech/mit-bestand-bericht:build --skip-nx-cache` — the real Zwischenbericht report (previously broken by the concurrent-session catcode bug above) now builds; its existing "Netzwerk" table (4 rows, fits on one page) rasterizes identically to before: "Tabelle: 0.a", no suffix, standard chrome.
- Built a throwaway fixture (verify-break.tex, run via build-verify.ts calling the same buildPrintDocument) with two short single-page Table/Figure windows plus one long, genuinely multi-page Table window (long-form paragraph content — a plain SemioTableThree/tabular is an atomic, unbreakable LaTeX box regardless of the window shell, so it cannot exercise page-splitting; unrelated to this ticket). Rasterized every page and confirmed: (a) the window border + header chip row repeats correctly on every one of 7 continuation page-parts; (b) hierarchy chip reads "Tabelle: 2.a:1" on page 1 (once recorded broken on a prior pass) through "Tabelle: 2.a:7" on the last part, no doubled suffixes; (c) two ordinary single-page windows elsewhere render with no suffix, identical chrome to a vanilla build; (d) .window-breaks aux file correctly records {1.a}{1}, {1.b}{1}, {2.a}{7}, {2.b}{1}.
- Could NOT get the list-of-tables register page to populate rows (header shows, body empty) — confirmed via a clean vanilla `report` template build that this is a pre-existing, unrelated bug (present for Figure/Photo/Image/Blockquote registers too, untouched by my change or the concurrent Termlist refactor). Spawned follow-up task task_d77ea2b5 for it instead of fixing under this ticket.

Deliberately out of scope / deferred:
- Generic `\Window` environment and `WindowRow`/`WindowColumn` arrangement primitives stay non-breakable (explicit `breakable=false` at their own call sites) — ticket's scenario is about "kind" windows (Table/Figure/etc.).
- Did not add breakability to `SemioTableThree`/`SemioTableTwo` (atomic `tabular`, cannot page-split regardless of shell) — only `SemioTableRegister`'s existing longtable mechanism (already-working, content-level, separate from window chrome per the ticket's own framing) splits row-by-row.

Files touched:
- print/tex/semio-window.sty (breakable windows, header-repeat overlay, two-pass part-suffix aux mechanism, concurrent-session catcode bug fix)
- print/script.ts (added `.window-breaks` to clearStaleTocAuxFiles)
- .repo/🎫/26/07/13/PRINT-WINDOW-PAGE-BREAK-SHELL-REPEAT-AND-PART-SUFFIX/verify-break.tex (new, throwaway verification fixture, kept per repo rules)
- .repo/🎫/26/07/13/PRINT-WINDOW-PAGE-BREAK-SHELL-REPEAT-AND-PART-SUFFIX/build-verify.ts (new, throwaway build runner for the fixture, kept per repo rules)
- .repo/🎫/26/07/13/PRINT-WINDOW-PAGE-BREAK-SHELL-REPEAT-AND-PART-SUFFIX/dist/* (build output of the fixture, kept per repo rules)

All of the above (including print/tex/semio-window.sty and print/script.ts) were captured by the repo's live auto-commit process during this session — confirmed via git log/git show that nothing was lost.
